name: VO2sday Micro Race (5 of 5) by Zwift Insider
description:
Welcome to VO2sday - 5 short, back-to-back TT races designed to give you a properly structured VO2 Max workout in a motivating and engaging race!

RESULTS: Final race results combining all 5 events can be found at https://leadoutesports.com/vo2sday/. 

IMPORTANT: You need to create an account at Leadout and link it to your Zwift account to show up in race results.

All races are 4 minutes long. Whoever rides the furthest, wins! Be sure to complete all 5 races so you get a full workout and are included in the overall competition.

Because the goal is for you to hold your max power for the duration of each race, these are set up as mass-start time trial events. Drafting is disabled, so there's no 'sitting in.' Use the best TT frame and wheels you've got. Push as hard as you can for the race duration, then recover and do it again!

Categories are based on your compound score, which takes into account your 5-minute power and body weight, computed as (5-min power in W/kg) * (5-min power in W). Current category setup:

- A: 1600+
- B: 1200-1600
- C: 900-1200
- D: 900 and below

name: Norwegian Watts Club BANDED social ride
description:
Welcome to Norwegian Watts Club social ride🙂

This ride is for all abilities--from first-timers to seasoned cyclists. Thanks to then banded ride feature, nobody gets left behind: as long as you keep pedaling, you'll stay with the group.
That means you can ride at your own pace,  focus on enjoying the route, and still be part of the bunch the whole way.

Our goal is simple: create a relaxed and supportive atmosphere where everyone feels at home. 
This ride isn't about Watts, KOMs, or race tactics-- it's about community,  good conversation,  and sharing the ride together.  Whether you're here to spin your legs,  make new Zwift friends,  or just enjoy some easy miles with like-minded rider, you'll find a warm welcome with the Norwegian Watts Club. 

What to Expect:

*All riders welcome -- no matter your pace or experience 

*Bande ride -- stick with the group just by pedaling 

*Social atmosphere  -- chat, laugh, encourage and ride together 

* A fun and supportive community 

So fire up Zwift, clip in and come ride with us.
It's not about how fast you go -- it's about who you ride with.

name: Mountain Massif Mini TT series - Race 1 s/b Hyperice
description:
This event is designed to replicate a prologue, which is a short individual time trial (ITT) held at the beginning of a stage race.

The race will test your ability to go "" full throttle " for a very short period of time and to push yourself beyond your perceived limits. On occasions, there will be a slightly longer time trial, where you can target hitting your best 20-minute power numbers.

With the same equipment being used, this is the ultimate “Race of truth” as a legendary commentator.
Phil Liggett described it.

There are three races on offer, which form part of a series where the overall winner will be the one who completes the three races, with the most accumulated points, which are awarded depending on your finishing position.

Alternatively, you can target one race and go for that individual win; the choice is yours. This event is sponsored by Hyperice.

About Hyperice:
They create innovative products that are designed to relieve tension, help sore muscles, and aid recovery. 

Founded in 2011 by Anthony Katz, Hyperice has worked to push the boundaries of innovation to
help better serve athletes everywhere.

Heart Rate monitor required and Zwift Power for official results, the winner of each category.

name: Run in the Park Group 5km's'
description:
Join us for a structured 5km progressive workout event, with each group targeting a
specific finish time so you can choose the effort that fits your goals.
-
Every group includes a progressive 5km run workout where the pace increases each
kilometre, finishing with a fast 400m free run to let you open up and push hard to the
line.
-
A warmup and cooldown segment is included, giving a total event distance of 6km
for Groups A, B and C with Groups D and E having a shorter warmup/cooldown
distance to slightly shorten the overall run to 5.4km and 5.6km respectively.
-
Group A: 5km in 20 minutes (600m warmup + 400m cooldown; 6.0km total)
-
Group B: 5km in 25 minutes (600m warmup + 400m cooldown; 6.0km total)
-
Group C: 5km in 30 minutes (600m warmup + 400m cooldown; 6.0km total)
-
Group D: 5km in 35 minutes (400m warmup + 200m cooldown; 5.6km total)
-
Group E: 5km in 40 minutes (200m warmup + 200m cooldown; 5.4km total)
-
Choose the group based on the time you want to run for your progressive 5km (not
including the warmup/cooldown). This is a workout event designed to allow people
to run together, not a race.
-
There is a 10-minute post-event cooldown period for chatting and congratulating
fellow runners
This is a great session for improving your 5km speed, practicing pacing discipline, or
simply enjoying a group workout with structure and purpose.

name: The Tour 21 Tuesday Social
description:
Welcome to The Tour 21 Tuesday Social, a social ride led by Ribble Cycles ambassadors Cam Jeffers and Katie Kookaburra. Join us to celebrate this year’s Tour 21, which sees 18 amateurs take on the full 2022 Tour de France route ahead of the pros with a mission to raise £1 million for Cure Leukaemia, the official charity partner of the Tour de France in the UK. All levels are welcome and we’re keeping things strictly social so we can all ride together (2.2 - 2.7 w/kg). Keep an eye on the ride leader’s yellow beacon to help keep the group together - ride sweepers will also help anyone get back on if they lose contact with the group.
It’s time to live the Tour, feel the Tour and ride the Tour!

name: Zwift Women's Training Club Workout
description:
Welcome to the Zwift Women’s Training Club workouts! 

ZWTC is your community for fun and fitness. Our weekly workouts will take you through some of Zwift’s most popular training plans, and with the flexibility to join in any time, regardless of where we are in the plan! Get the most out of your Zwifting with training designed by world-class coaches, like 3x Olympic Gold medalist, Kristin Armstrong!

The group workouts will be held every 3 hours UTC on Tuesdays and Thursdays. We’ll also offer recovery rides every 3 hours on Wednesdays - be on the look out for special guests joining those! Our main goal is to provide you with a consistent experience week in and week out, to challenge yourself in a supportive group setting, making friends and getting fit along the way! 

Join the Zwift Women’s Training Club to connect with new ride friends, ask questions, and get advice from experts.  https://www.zwift.com/clubs/ZwiftWTC/join

Love these workouts? Check out the club for more opportunities to train with us! We offer social rides every 3 hours on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays in addition to the Tuesday/Thursday workouts.

name: ROAD TO ZWIFT RACING LEAGUE
description:
Team up. Show up. Race together.

Zwift Racing League is team racing at its best: fast, sweaty, and addictive. Race alongside your teammates every Tuesday, combining teamwork, tactics, and competition with the kind of Type 2 Fun that keeps you coming back for more.

The 2026/27 season features four 6-week rounds from September to April, with new routes, a new format, XP rewards, and exclusive unlocks along the way. Round 1 gets underway on September 22.

YOUR ROAD TO ZRL STARTS HERE

Thinking about racing ZRL? This group ride is designed to show you what it’s all about and help you get ready for the start line.
Ride alongside other Zwifters as we introduce you to team racing, what to expect when you race ZRL, and how to take the next step and join a team.

There’s no racing today. Just ride with the group, learn more about ZRL, and get ready to race together.

READY TO RACE?

Once you've completed the ride, the next step is to find your team and get signed up.

Getting started is simple:

1 - Create your WTRL profile by connecting your Zwift account.
2 - Visit the ZRL Find a Team page for ways to find a team.
3 - Or register your own team and invite your friends.

REGISTER NOW
https://www.wtrl.racing/zwift-racing-league/

description:

There is no better way to get more comfortable climbing than with a fun & supportive group! Get stronger and meet your fitness targets with Velos.

name: SISU Punainen - Stage 4
description:
SISU Racing launches its boldest challenge yet: SISU Punainen, a Vuelta-inspired, seven-stage race series built for riders who thrive when the road tilts skyward. Set entirely in Watopia, this inaugural edition is unapologetically brutal, beautifully relentless, and designed for the mountain goats of the virtual peloton.

Riders will compete for three individual classifications, ensuring every stage offers something to race for. The coveted Punainen (red in FInnish) Jersey rewards the overall General Classification leader based on cumulative elapsed time across all seven stages. The Sprintteri Jersey recognises the fastest riders through the designated sprint segments, while the Vuorikauris (Mountain Goat) Jersey celebrates the strongest climbers.  Whether you're an all-rounder, a sprinter or a pure climber, there's a jersey to chase.
Just like the Vuelta, SISU Punainen rewards courage, consistency, and climbing prowess.

For more information, and results, visit sisu.racing/punainen.

The Stages

Stage 1
Hilly Route, Watopia (Individual Time Trial)
Sat 22 & Sun 23 August

Stage 2
Mayan San Remo, Watopia
Tue 25 & Wed 26 August

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 3
Three Little Sisters, Watopia
Sat 29 & Sun 30 August

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 4
Climbers Gambit, Watopia
Tue 1 & Wed 2 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 5
Big Loop, Watopia
Sat 5 & Sun 6 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 6
Mountain 8, Watopia
Tue 8 & Wed 9 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 7
Mountain Route, Watopia
Sat 12 & Sun 13 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather, Aero or Anvil


Zwift Race Score

In our ongoing effort to keep the racing scene fresh and competitive, the upcoming SISU Punainen series is embracing Zwift's flexible new Zwift Racing Score (ZRS) framework!
Following a format similar to the recent Zwift Tour Fever series, this shift away from standard Category boundaries allows us to create tighter, more closely matched fields.

What this means for you:

A Shakeup in the Pack: If you usually find yourself stuck in the middle of a traditional category, this is your chance to step up, animate the race, and battle for the win.
New Challenges for Front-Runners: Former category leaders will be pushed to find new limits against a freshly recalibrated field.
Dynamic Racing Throughout: While the elite action in A Grade will remain as fierce as ever, expect highly competitive, unpredictable, and dynamic racing across the board - especially in Cat D Grade and expanded E Grade!

A Grade: 701-1000
B Grade: 551-700
C Grade: 401-550
D Grade: 251-400
E Grade: 1-250

The Jerseys

The General Classification (GC) is decided by the cumulative elapsed time taken to complete all seven stages. The Team Classification is based on the combined time of each team's fastest three riders on every stage.
The Sprintteri and Vuorikauris (Mountain Goat) classifications are determined by a rider's cumulative time through all designated Sprint and KOM/QOM segments of Stages 2 to 7. Where a stage includes the same segment multiple times, only the rider's fastest time through that segment will count toward the classification.

The Johtaja (leader in Finnish) classification is decided by the cumulative elapsed time taken to complete all seven stages in each age category.

Upgrade Information

Riders who upgrade during the first six stages will be classified in their higher grade.  Riders who upgrade in Stage 7 will not be re-classified.

Further Information

Open events using Zwift’s Racing Score with separate results for Men and Women.
Each event is a mass start with all riders visible on the course.
TT bikes are mandatory for the iTT. Draft will be disabled.
Z Power and riders without heart rate data will be excluded from the results.
A rider's best time will count if they race the same stage in multiple zones.
To be included in the GC riders must have a Zwiftpower profile.
Team GC will be based on each team’s fastest three riders.

name: Team Rynkeby - Europe's most meaningful cycling team!
description:
In Bologna, the prolog for 2019 Giro d'Italia awaits.
We begin at Piazza Maggiore, which is the main square in the heart of Bologna. Other sights here include the Basilica di San Petronio and Fountain of Neptune.
Next, we cover some cobbled streets lined with arcades, past Porta San Felice (the westernmost gate of medieval Bologna).
The climb begins at Arco del Meloncello with a sharp right hairpin. You’ll know you’re halfway up the climb when you hit another right hairpin and go under the stone arch. When you see the Sanctuary of the Madonna di San Luca you’ll know you’re almost there. And when you see the giant Scottie inflatable, give it all you’ve got over the line!
And then we turn around, ride back to the starting point, and do it all again :-D
- An important element of Team Rynkeby’s work is raising money for organisations that support children with critical illnesses. The money is raised from a variety of sources including sponsorships from generous businesses. Team Rynkeby is a voluntary initiative, which means that we rely on sponsors to supply many of the things we need for our trip. This includes vehicles, fuel, food and beverages. Our participants pay their own way via the participation fee. Via its three brands – Rynkeby, God Morgon and hohes C – the German juice group, Eckes-Granini covers the major costs of the project in cooperation with the organisations for which the money is raised. This means that all the money raised is donated to organisations that help children with critical illnesses. Join our Discord-channel: https://discord.gg/dVvd7azK6s

name: VTTA 10 miles Time Trial
description:
Zwift VTTA Ten Mile TT series

Join in with the VTTA (Veterans Time Trials Association) for a classic time trial on Zwift! This 10-mile TT is a true test of your power and pacing. Push your limits and see how you stack up against other riders in a race against the clock. See how your times compare week on week through the series.

About the VTTA

The Veterans Time Trials Association (VTTA) is an organization for cyclists aged 40 and over who are interested in time trials. The VTTA uses a unique ""age-adjusted"" handicapping system to level the playing field for riders of all ages to allow for fair regardless of their age. The VTTA also maintains national age records and organizes various competitions and championships in real life.

Event Details:

Distance: 10 miles (16.1 km)
Format: Time Trial
Bike: TT bikes are allowed and highly recommended

Important Notes:

This is a time trial, so drafting is disabled.
Power-ups are also disabled to ensure a fair and pure test of your fitness.
Smart trainer or a Power Meter must be used. Sorry no ZPower users

Please ensure your ZwiftPower account is connected to your Zwift account for accurate results. If you are a VTTA member remember to put VTTA and your membership number after your name in ZPower so we can put your results in the league tables..

Get ready to suffer and set a new personal best! Good luck!

name: Wahooligan Official Group Workout
description:

This workout is focused on aerobic conditioning, getting your aerobic system revved up for some harder training session ahead. In this workout we accumulate a total of 30min 'work' with the majority of that below your FTP. We split this workout into x3 10min segments but within each segment we have x2 1 min bursts above FTP. These 1min bursts rise from 102% up to 107% over the 3 blocks.

name: TOUR HISP 2026 Stage 8
description:
Tour de HISP 2026

This is HISP’s most challenging and exigent event, now in its fifth edition.

We will race 13 stages in 14 days, starting on August 24th. There will be four starts each day, so you can choose whichever fits your schedule best. You can even repeat a stage, but only your best time will count for the General Classification (GC).

Standings will be calculated by simple time addition, just like a classic stage race. Categories will be assigned according to the ZCE system.

You can find more information on the stages and schedule here: https://hispevents.com

You can find the GC (ZwiftPower) here: https://zwiftpower.com/league.php?id=3324

***

Tour de HISP 2026

Este es el evento más exigente de HISP, nuestro mayor desafío, que llega ya a su quinta edición.

Serán trece etapas en catorce días, arrancando el 24 de agosto. Contaremos con cuatro salidas diarias para que puedas escoger la que mejor te convenga. Puedes repetir la etapa si lo deseas, pero solamente contará tu mejor tiempo para la Clasificación General (GC).

La clasificación se calculará por suma simple de tiempos, como en una carrera clásica por etapas. Las categorías se regirán por el sistema ZCE.

Puedes encontrar toda la información sobre el evento y las etapas aquí: https://hispevents.com

Puedes encontrar la Clasificación General (ZwiftPower) aquí: https://zwiftpower.com/league.php?id=3324

name: ROAD TO ZWIFT RACING LEAGUE
description:
Team up. Show up. Race together.

Zwift Racing League is team racing at its best: fast, sweaty, and addictive. Race alongside your teammates every Tuesday, combining teamwork, tactics, and competition with the kind of Type 2 Fun that keeps you coming back for more.

The 2026/27 season features four 6-week rounds from September to April, with new routes, a new format, XP rewards, and exclusive unlocks along the way. Round 1 gets underway on September 22.

YOUR ROAD TO ZRL STARTS HERE

Thinking about racing ZRL? This group ride is designed to show you what it’s all about and help you get ready for the start line.
Ride alongside other Zwifters as we introduce you to team racing, what to expect when you race ZRL, and how to take the next step and join a team.

There’s no racing today. Just ride with the group, learn more about ZRL, and get ready to race together.

READY TO RACE?

Once you've completed the ride, the next step is to find your team and get signed up.

Getting started is simple:

1 - Create your WTRL profile by connecting your Zwift account.
2 - Visit the ZRL Find a Team page for ways to find a team.
3 - Or register your own team and invite your friends.

name: JETT Warm up Ride for JZMR (2.5~3.0w/kg)
description:
JETT Warming up Ride for JZMR
Power ave. 2.5w/kg to 3.0w/kg
JZMR=JETT Zwift Morning Race will start 15 minutes after the end of this event. Of course, all ZWIFTers are welcome to participate. Leaders and front riders will lead the group with 2.5 to 3.0w/kg. Riders who have a hard time with the above power can try grouping by making good use of drafting.
If you are far behind the group, please say "HELP! at the ZWIFT CAHT and Sweeper will come to your aid. Unless you say "HELP! Sweeper will not go to your aid unless you say "HELP! If at all possible, please do so within 10 seconds of each other.
Rules for this group ride
1)Keep the grouping in mind at all times (this is not a race).
2)Do not go further than the leader's yellow beacon (20m or more)
3)TT Bikes can be used, but they do not provide a drafting effect.
4)Follow the leader's instruction for sprint.
30 minute Group Ride, follow the leader's instructions, and work together to make it a great group and a great workout!

Please join to our Facebook page.
https://www.facebook.com/groups/zwiftjett/

・TT Bikeは使用可能ですが、ドラフティング効果を得られません。
・スプリントはリーダー指示に従ってください。
30分のGroup Ride、リーダー指示に従い、みんなで協力して最高のグループ、最高のワークアウトにしましょう！

皆さんをFacebookページでお待ちしております！

name: GGCC Glasgow Green CC Tuesday Training ride
description:
GGCC group rides are TRAINING events, category C, with a yellow beacon leader. The beacon leader will ride to 2.5w/kg pace average wherever possible.

Please look out for our training rides 3 days a week, every week - Tuesdays at 20.45 UTC, Thursdays at 21.00 UTC and Saturdays at 11.30am UTC. Use #ggcc to search, as in https://zwift.com/events/tag/ggcc

The Glasgow Green Cycle Club (GGCC) training rides are intended to provide a challenge for riders, and are open to all timezones. You should ride as a group, following the instructions of the beacon ride leader(s) for any sprints, intervals and spicy segments, regrouping after each when requested. All our group rides also have a closing minirace, to start from behind the beacon.

GGCC is a Glasgow based cycling club whose “in real life” (irl) club runs and training rides are always organized into pace groups, which match the Zwift categories quite well. GGCC also has a good race pedigree and presence in Scotland, and so we have organized this training ride series to suit what we believe is relevant to bike riders’ interests in performance and improvement in our club, in other Glasgow clubs, in Scotland and the UK. Racers will, no doubt, aspire to try our other events, both our Monday 20.10 UTC Zwift races, and our Friday 19.45 UTC TTs.

As we expect our club’s riders to be able to ride 50 miles at a 15mph average on our Sunday rides, such steady riding members will be comfortable with Zwift Category C, and in our various rides we cater for all abilities, through the Zwift ABCD levels. Beacon leaders communicate via Zwift messaging (always) and/or Discord (sometimes) to vary the pace to allow for sprints, intervals, and optionally a mini-race towards the end of the rides, with regrouping after each segment. Make as much use of drafting as you can, for more effective sprinting and intervals.

Results can be seen at the end of the ride on screen, and we will, in common with many other ride series, publish your results on zwiftpower.com too, based on each category.

All bikes and PUs are allowed, but better not to use TT bikes (which don’t draft) on our group rides and races. Please add GGCC (X) to your Zwift name to allow your ride presence to be recognized, where X is your desired ride category. Categories are related to your Functional Threshold Power (FTP); use your FTP and then divide by your weight in kg, then pick the correct ride and group.

C: 2 W/kg to 3 W/kg FTP; the beacon leader will ride to 2.5w/kg pace average.

PLEASE NOTE: Strava data for our rides must be open (not private or hidden). Please use a heart monitor so that we can monitor correlated power and heart rate to help assure fair riding.
You can use our Discord channel to talk to each other at https://discord.gg/UDhdEQA
Please see the GGCC Zwift page link at http://www.glasgowgreencycleclub.co.uk/ for more.

For more about specific Zwift courses for our events, see the Zwift Companion schedule, and also https://zwiftinsider.com/ where there is a wealth of information about all things Zwift.

#ggcc

name: AHDR Bacon Rolls with Caffeine
description:
Welcome to AHDR Bacon Rolls with Caffeine.
It’s hump day morning and should you need something a little extra to get you through to the weekend, you’ve come to the right place!

We ride with the beacons for the first part of the event enjoying the blobbiness and banter that AHDR brings with a pace around 2.5-3.0W/kg. Then just before the last lap/s, you have a decision to make - race the CAFFEINE lap or join the RED beacon to finish the event at pre-caffeine pace.

There's even a lower grade version (without the racing) with the "D-Caff" group, that starts 5 mins later. It really is an event with something for everyone!

Have a blast, have a laugh, and enjoy the fun that is AHDR Bacon Rolls, but with a splash of CAFFEINE! Should you sleep in, or hit snooze, you may Join/Rejoin for up to 30 minutes.

name: TPR Pelo x Attaquer - Maeve Plouffe
description:
For this week's ride we are partnering with the Attaquer crew who will be joining TPR Pelo ride! There will be a sweet Attaquer prize pack up for grabs during the ride so make sure you bunch up to the beacon and stay close to Jethro (hint, hint)

The Pelo is an easy 60-minute weekly ride where we can talk a bit about our favourite Aussie cyclists and how they are going over in Europe and start some discussions as to what we think will happen in the upcoming races each week. The ride will automatically play the latest episode of The Press Room Podcast presented by Zwift so, if you prefer to simply listen and pedal then you are more than welcome to tag along with us and be apart of the community!

The Press Room Podcast is a cycling podcast featuring extended interviews with some of the world's best cyclists, key staff personnel and other notable cycling personalities. Through thought provoking and casual "on the couch" interviews, The Press Room pulls back the curtains on professional cyclists to highlight the stories, relationships and characters that are often hidden beyond the results sheet.

The Press Room Podcast presented by Zwift is available for download on all podcast players such as Spotify, Apple and Google podcasts. Be sure to subscribe to the pod and follow the Instagram and Youtube channel for all the latest updates.

Join The Press Room Pelo CC Zwift Club!

Episode 8 of TPR features Australia's most exciting prospect on the track and on the road - Maeve Plouffe. Maeve runs us through her recent success at the Track Nationals (despite some challenges) where she won back the IP title, her World Tour ambitions on the road for 2023 and we discuss how she got into the sport before diving deep in to the art of sprinting and who inspires her as a female athlete.

The Press Room podcast is presented by our title sponsor Zwift.

name: Zwift Women's Training Club Workout
description:
Welcome to the Zwift Women’s Training Club workouts! 

ZWTC is your community for fun and fitness. Our weekly workouts will take you through some of Zwift’s most popular training plans, and with the flexibility to join in any time, regardless of where we are in the plan! Get the most out of your Zwifting with training designed by world-class coaches, like 3x Olympic Gold medalist, Kristin Armstrong!

The group workouts will be held every 3 hours UTC on Tuesdays and Thursdays. We’ll also offer recovery rides every 3 hours on Wednesdays - be on the look out for special guests joining those! Our main goal is to provide you with a consistent experience week in and week out, to challenge yourself in a supportive group setting, making friends and getting fit along the way! 

Join the Zwift Women’s Training Club to connect with new ride friends, ask questions, and get advice from experts.  https://www.zwift.com/clubs/ZwiftWTC/join

Love these workouts? Check out the club for more opportunities to train with us! We offer social rides every 3 hours on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays in addition to the Tuesday/Thursday workouts.

name: ROAD TO ZWIFT RACING LEAGUE
description:
Team up. Show up. Race together.

Zwift Racing League is team racing at its best: fast, sweaty, and addictive. Race alongside your teammates every Tuesday, combining teamwork, tactics, and competition with the kind of Type 2 Fun that keeps you coming back for more.

The 2026/27 season features four 6-week rounds from September to April, with new routes, a new format, XP rewards, and exclusive unlocks along the way. Round 1 gets underway on September 22.

YOUR ROAD TO ZRL STARTS HERE

Thinking about racing ZRL? This group ride is designed to show you what it’s all about and help you get ready for the start line.
Ride alongside other Zwifters as we introduce you to team racing, what to expect when you race ZRL, and how to take the next step and join a team.

There’s no racing today. Just ride with the group, learn more about ZRL, and get ready to race together.

READY TO RACE?

Once you've completed the ride, the next step is to find your team and get signed up.

Getting started is simple:

1 - Create your WTRL profile by connecting your Zwift account.
2 - Visit the ZRL Find a Team page for ways to find a team.
3 - Or register your own team and invite your friends.

REGISTER NOW
https://www.wtrl.racing/zwift-racing-league/

name: SISU Punainen - Stage 4
description:
SISU Racing launches its boldest challenge yet: SISU Punainen, a Vuelta-inspired, seven-stage race series built for riders who thrive when the road tilts skyward. Set entirely in Watopia, this inaugural edition is unapologetically brutal, beautifully relentless, and designed for the mountain goats of the virtual peloton.

Riders will compete for three individual classifications, ensuring every stage offers something to race for. The coveted Punainen (red in FInnish) Jersey rewards the overall General Classification leader based on cumulative elapsed time across all seven stages. The Sprintteri Jersey recognises the fastest riders through the designated sprint segments, while the Vuorikauris (Mountain Goat) Jersey celebrates the strongest climbers.  Whether you're an all-rounder, a sprinter or a pure climber, there's a jersey to chase.
Just like the Vuelta, SISU Punainen rewards courage, consistency, and climbing prowess.

For more information, and results, visit sisu.racing/punainen.

The Stages

Stage 1
Hilly Route, Watopia (Individual Time Trial)
Sat 22 & Sun 23 August

Stage 2
Mayan San Remo, Watopia
Tue 25 & Wed 26 August

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 3
Three Little Sisters, Watopia
Sat 29 & Sun 30 August

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 4
Climbers Gambit, Watopia
Tue 1 & Wed 2 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 5
Big Loop, Watopia
Sat 5 & Sun 6 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 6
Mountain 8, Watopia
Tue 8 & Wed 9 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 7
Mountain Route, Watopia
Sat 12 & Sun 13 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather, Aero or Anvil


Zwift Race Score

In our ongoing effort to keep the racing scene fresh and competitive, the upcoming SISU Punainen series is embracing Zwift's flexible new Zwift Racing Score (ZRS) framework!
Following a format similar to the recent Zwift Tour Fever series, this shift away from standard Category boundaries allows us to create tighter, more closely matched fields.

What this means for you:

A Shakeup in the Pack: If you usually find yourself stuck in the middle of a traditional category, this is your chance to step up, animate the race, and battle for the win.
New Challenges for Front-Runners: Former category leaders will be pushed to find new limits against a freshly recalibrated field.
Dynamic Racing Throughout: While the elite action in A Grade will remain as fierce as ever, expect highly competitive, unpredictable, and dynamic racing across the board - especially in Cat D Grade and expanded E Grade!

A Grade: 701-1000
B Grade: 551-700
C Grade: 401-550
D Grade: 251-400
E Grade: 1-250

The Jerseys

The General Classification (GC) is decided by the cumulative elapsed time taken to complete all seven stages. The Team Classification is based on the combined time of each team's fastest three riders on every stage.
The Sprintteri and Vuorikauris (Mountain Goat) classifications are determined by a rider's cumulative time through all designated Sprint and KOM/QOM segments of Stages 2 to 7. Where a stage includes the same segment multiple times, only the rider's fastest time through that segment will count toward the classification.

The Johtaja (leader in Finnish) classification is decided by the cumulative elapsed time taken to complete all seven stages in each age category.

Upgrade Information

Riders who upgrade during the first six stages will be classified in their higher grade.  Riders who upgrade in Stage 7 will not be re-classified.

Further Information

Open events using Zwift’s Racing Score with separate results for Men and Women.
Each event is a mass start with all riders visible on the course.
TT bikes are mandatory for the iTT. Draft will be disabled.
Z Power and riders without heart rate data will be excluded from the results.
A rider's best time will count if they race the same stage in multiple zones.
To be included in the GC riders must have a Zwiftpower profile.
Team GC will be based on each team’s fastest three riders.

name: Ride to End ALZ
description:
The Ride to End ALZ South Carolina is a three-day, cross-state journey for cycling enthusiasts. Now in its 18th year, the unique Group Ride travels from beautiful Upstate South Carolina to the picturesque Charleston coast July 10-12, 2026. Riders may choose between two mileage options: The Grand Tour (257 miles) or The Half Tour (136 miles). This event is known for its incredible support along the route and camaraderie that only a multi-day ride can bring. Participants may also ride at their own pace from anywhere in our month-long Virtual Challenge. Either way, funds raised by riders benefit the Alzheimer's Association and fuel cutting-edge research targeted to change the trajectory of Alzheimer’s disease.
Get all the details at alz.org/ridesc

This Zwift ride is open to everyone and all paces, and our goal is to fill you in on the details of the incredible impact Ride to End ALZ has on making progress towards the research and treatment of Alzheimers through funding with the Alzheimer’s Association. In addition to the 3-day Group Ride in SC, there is also a month-long Virtual Challenge option! Join us, unlock the Ride to End ALZ kit, and learn more about how YOU can make a difference in the fight against Alzheimer’s! Join our Facebook group to get all the latest info: https://www.facebook.com/groups/alzRTR
More details at alz.org/ridesc

name: DIRT Family Values Ride
description:
Welcome to the DIRT Family Values Ride

Please join us weekly on Tuesday evenings for a 1.5 – 1.8 w/kg 50 minute group ride. 

Our yellow beacon group leader will remain in the 1.5 - 1.8 w/kg range for the entirety of the ride. This is a social ride.  All are welcome to join. Please follow the yellow beacon at all times.

Team DIRT is an acronym for Dads Inside Riding Trainers. We are a brotherhood like-minded moms and dads who love to make time for Zwift around work and family. We are a social racing team consisting mostly of mid-level Zwifters. The Family Values Ride idea came about because a lot of us have work and family obligations during the week and this would be a perfect way to squeeze in a great ride.

Don't forget to add "DIRT" after your name and make sure you are not on a TT bike.
 
Please join us on Discord at https://discord.gg/sUnwqPZ
 
And, Facebook at https://www.facebook.com/groups/ZWIFTDIRT
 
Also, find us at IndoorSpecialist.com

name: Giant Tuesday Ride Series
description:

name: Faster Masters B & C Group Ride
description:
Tuesday’s ride includes B and C Category Groups (teams). Ride concept is two-fold: Group B departs first. Group C starts one minute later. Group B will maintain a steady pace unless directed otherwise by the yellow beacon (team leader). Group C will also maintain a steady pace unless directed otherwise by the yellow beacon. This ride offers C level riders the opportunity to train at a higher level if they wish by starting with Group B for a period of time, then fall back with Group C to complete the ride. Doing so week after week riders can try to stay in the faster group longer each week until they are able to remain with Group B for the entire event. Start times: Group B, 6:00 PM, ET (New York Time); Group C beginning at 6:01 PM. The pace efforts for Group C will be from 2.5 to 3.1 w/kg; Group B’s pace effort is 3.2 to 4.0 w/kg. This ride setup is also a good format should Freebirds (flyers) join Group C; the yellow beacon can advise Freebirds to either return to the group or attack trying to catch Group B ahead. If utilized, this should be done early in the ride. 

Both groups include a 30-minute Late Join period. During this time, dropped riders can use the Late Join feature to rejoin. If you find that the group you selected is either too fast or too slow for your pace, you can use Late Join to switch groups within the first 30 minutes of the start time of the group you would like to join. 

We do not sweep during the first 30 minutes of a ride. If you fall behind for any reason during this time, we recommend using Late Join to re-join near the yellow beacon position. We usually do not have designated sweepers (Red Beacon). After the first 30 minutes, if you get dropped and want to rejoin your group, please send a message in the format HELP(X), where X is the number of seconds you are off the back (for example, HELP5). If you reach out early, one or more stronger riders may come to assist you. If a sweep is needed we recommend you message HELP within 10 seconds.

name: Triathletes on Zwift Tuesday High Intensity Workout
description:
ABOUT THIS WORKOUT

This workout is part of a 24-week progressive series that builds from All Out to Super Threshold efforts over subsequent weeks.  The All-Out efforts aid to develop rider's top end aerobic abilities to push big wattage for relatively short periods of time with controlled rest periods.  The All Out and Super/Sub Threshold efforts allow riders to focus on improving their ability to ride at or slightly above their FTP for extended periods of time, again with fairly moderate rest intervals.  Workouts begin with a warm up period  where riders will go through short progressive builds towards the workouts goal FTP percentage.  A main set of intervals will follow that focuse on developing aerobic capacity.  Each of the 24-week workouts builds off the preceding workout in terms of duration of main set intervals.

WORKOUT DESIGNER

AJ Baucco is a well established professional triathlete from Cleveland, Ohio. He founded AJ Baucco Coaching, which has coached over 150 triathletes in the last 5 years. He also manages 3 different age group triathlon teams; The Baucco Squad, TRS Racing, and Team INFINIT Performance. Over the years, AJ Baucco has become a premier triathlon coach. He has helped athletes achieve personal bests, stand on podiums, and even race world championship events. On the race course, AJ Baucco has achieved top results at every distance from super sprint to Ironman. Most recently, he was on the winning team for 6 different Major League Triathlon events, and 2 back to back series championships.

Contact – 
Websites – www.baucco.com, www.ajbcoaching.com, www.bauccosquad.com
Twitter - @irunshirtless
Instagram - @ajbaucco

ABOUT GROUP WORKOUTS

Zwifters line up in the starting area just like a normal event and once the event starts, workout mode begins.  Everyone stays together regardless of power output.   That's right, if you're outputting 100W and another Zwifter is outputting 400W you will stay in exactly the same position relative to each other.  Only if you stop pedaling and fall 6 meters behind the group will the rubber-banding stop.

HELPFUL HINT

We highly recommend doing one of the FTP tests as the estimated FTP can be inaccurate and make the difficulty level of the workouts too high for your current fitness level.   

For more info on FTP go to: https://support.zwift.com/hc/en-us/articles/210208083-What-is-FTP-and-how-is-it-used-in-Zwift

name: Phoenix Rising United
description:
The Phoenix Rising United ride is designed to leave the stresses of the day behind us. We're here for you to help you turn your day around, or to make a great day shine even brighter. We are here for your recovery, warm up/cool down, or threshold workout. Whatever your reasons are, we've got you covered. Our average pace is 26-30kph (16-19mph) with power target average of 1.4 to 1.7 W/kg, and our leaders will not exceed those paces regardless of the route. The leader has the option to activate the no-kick fence to visually guide riders to understand where their position is relative to the leader. Our objective, as with all Phoenix Rising group rides, is to share some friendly banter and enjoy the camaraderie. We employ a fabulous group of sweepers to accompany and/or help riders rejoin the main yellow group. We intend that no one ride alone, unless they want to do so.

We will ride a variety of routes, mainly flatter routes, but we will occasionally do some fun climbing to add a little spice. Please feel free to suggest a route you would like to try sometime, or a badge you need that can be completed in a 60-minute time period. We're happy to add suggestions to the ride list.

For more information on all our weekly events, join our club Phoenix Rising on Zwift Companion.

name: Zwift Crit Racing Club - Mech Isle Loop
description:
It's Crit time! Come and join in the fun on a number of multi-lap short routes. Get ready to dig deep and push to the finish line!

What is Racing Score?

Racing Score is an intuitive system that replaces the traditional categories (A - D) with a 0-1000 scale to reflect your current level, considering various metrics like race performances and power. This score helps Zwift recommend the most competitive band to race in, ensuring a fun, rewarding, and exciting experience as you track your progression throughout your Zwift racing adventures.

WHAT IS ZWIFT POWER? For further information on connecting to Zwift Power check out this support page: https://support.zwift.com/en_us/connecting-to-zwiftpower-SyldRc_4H

Please note; for your results to show up in Zwift Power you must be using a Heart Rate Monitor (HRM) and be riding on a smart trainer, smart bike, or using a power meter.

name: VO2sday Micro Race (1 of 5) by Zwift Insider
description:
Welcome to VO2sday - 5 short, back-to-back TT races designed to give you a properly structured VO2 Max workout in a motivating and engaging race!

RESULTS: Final race results combining all 5 events can be found at https://leadoutesports.com/vo2sday/. 

IMPORTANT: You need to create an account at Leadout and link it to your Zwift account to show up in race results.

All races are 4 minutes long. Whoever rides the furthest, wins! Be sure to complete all 5 races so you get a full workout and are included in the overall competition.

Because the goal is for you to hold your max power for the duration of each race, these are set up as mass-start time trial events. Drafting is disabled, so there's no 'sitting in.' Use the best TT frame and wheels you've got. Push as hard as you can for the race duration, then recover and do it again!

Categories are based on your compound score, which takes into account your 5-minute power and body weight, computed as (5-min power in W/kg) * (5-min power in W). Current category setup:

- A: 1600+
- B: 1200-1600
- C: 900-1200
- D: 900 and below

eventSubgroups.description:
Welcome to the USMES Warm-up Ride.
This is one of two weekly warm-up rides, with the goal of working from this group into the next ride with a higher pace. Use this ride to help you build that solid base for your training to build on!!
These Rides are generally low key and to socialize with our members. The group set up and pace is
specifically lower to support and train for our faster groups.
Pace will start off around 1.5w/kg and could work up to 2.5w/kg on hills. With the average pace being near 2w/kg. There may be times, when traversing a hill/bump, where the pace may go higher, but overall we should be around 2w/kg.
New to our rides or to Zwift? The best place to hang-out in the ride is in the front 1/3 of the Yellow Beacons (Leaders) Peloton or Blob. This keeps you in the draft and at the advertised pace and involved with the group.
The Fence will be used if necessary to control the group.
Please don’t chase the flyers, don’t encourage them. You joined the Group ride, then ride with the group. If you are dead set on Flying, then after the ride starts, select quite the ride and you will stay on the rides route and the Fence won’t zap you! Another option is if you have the energy and legs for it, volunteer SWEEP. Help those that need a wheel back to the blob and get your Interval work in for the day!!

Tour de HISP 2026

Este es el evento más exigente de HISP, nuestro mayor desafío, que llega ya a su quinta edición.

name: ROAD TO ZWIFT RACING LEAGUE
description:
Team up. Show up. Race together.

Zwift Racing League is team racing at its best: fast, sweaty, and addictive. Race alongside your teammates every Tuesday, combining teamwork, tactics, and competition with the kind of Type 2 Fun that keeps you coming back for more.

The 2026/27 season features four 6-week rounds from September to April, with new routes, a new format, XP rewards, and exclusive unlocks along the way. Round 1 gets underway on September 22.

YOUR ROAD TO ZRL STARTS HERE

Thinking about racing ZRL? This group ride is designed to show you what it’s all about and help you get ready for the start line.
Ride alongside other Zwifters as we introduce you to team racing, what to expect when you race ZRL, and how to take the next step and join a team.

There’s no racing today. Just ride with the group, learn more about ZRL, and get ready to race together.

READY TO RACE?

Once you've completed the ride, the next step is to find your team and get signed up.

Getting started is simple:

1 - Create your WTRL profile by connecting your Zwift account.
2 - Visit the ZRL Find a Team page for ways to find a team.
3 - Or register your own team and invite your friends.

REGISTER NOW
https://www.wtrl.racing/zwift-racing-league/

name: VO2sday Micro Race (2 of 5) by Zwift Insider
description:
Welcome to VO2sday - 5 short, back-to-back TT races designed to give you a properly structured VO2 Max workout in a motivating and engaging race!

RESULTS: Final race results combining all 5 events can be found at https://leadoutesports.com/vo2sday/. 

IMPORTANT: You need to create an account at Leadout and link it to your Zwift account to show up in race results.

All races are 4 minutes long. Whoever rides the furthest, wins! Be sure to complete all 5 races so you get a full workout and are included in the overall competition.

Because the goal is for you to hold your max power for the duration of each race, these are set up as mass-start time trial events. Drafting is disabled, so there's no 'sitting in.' Use the best TT frame and wheels you've got. Push as hard as you can for the race duration, then recover and do it again!

Categories are based on your compound score, which takes into account your 5-minute power and body weight, computed as (5-min power in W/kg) * (5-min power in W). Current category setup:

- A: 1600+
- B: 1200-1600
- C: 900-1200
- D: 900 and below

description:
All Zwifters are welcome to join the Ride to Conquer Cancer Training ride dedicated to conquering cancer.

This is a positive and inclusive ride - use it as a training or recovery ride and get social!

Like the 2-day, 200+ KM event in June every year, this is a ride, not a race. Challenge others in a sprint and then drop back with the group to socialize.

name: SISU Punainen - Stage 4
description:
SISU Racing launches its boldest challenge yet: SISU Punainen, a Vuelta-inspired, seven-stage race series built for riders who thrive when the road tilts skyward. Set entirely in Watopia, this inaugural edition is unapologetically brutal, beautifully relentless, and designed for the mountain goats of the virtual peloton.

Riders will compete for three individual classifications, ensuring every stage offers something to race for. The coveted Punainen (red in FInnish) Jersey rewards the overall General Classification leader based on cumulative elapsed time across all seven stages. The Sprintteri Jersey recognises the fastest riders through the designated sprint segments, while the Vuorikauris (Mountain Goat) Jersey celebrates the strongest climbers.  Whether you're an all-rounder, a sprinter or a pure climber, there's a jersey to chase.
Just like the Vuelta, SISU Punainen rewards courage, consistency, and climbing prowess.

For more information, and results, visit sisu.racing/punainen.

The Stages

Stage 1
Hilly Route, Watopia (Individual Time Trial)
Sat 22 & Sun 23 August

Stage 2
Mayan San Remo, Watopia
Tue 25 & Wed 26 August

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 3
Three Little Sisters, Watopia
Sat 29 & Sun 30 August

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 4
Climbers Gambit, Watopia
Tue 1 & Wed 2 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 5
Big Loop, Watopia
Sat 5 & Sun 6 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 6
Mountain 8, Watopia
Tue 8 & Wed 9 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 7
Mountain Route, Watopia
Sat 12 & Sun 13 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather, Aero or Anvil


Zwift Race Score

In our ongoing effort to keep the racing scene fresh and competitive, the upcoming SISU Punainen series is embracing Zwift's flexible new Zwift Racing Score (ZRS) framework!
Following a format similar to the recent Zwift Tour Fever series, this shift away from standard Category boundaries allows us to create tighter, more closely matched fields.

What this means for you:

A Shakeup in the Pack: If you usually find yourself stuck in the middle of a traditional category, this is your chance to step up, animate the race, and battle for the win.
New Challenges for Front-Runners: Former category leaders will be pushed to find new limits against a freshly recalibrated field.
Dynamic Racing Throughout: While the elite action in A Grade will remain as fierce as ever, expect highly competitive, unpredictable, and dynamic racing across the board - especially in Cat D Grade and expanded E Grade!

A Grade: 701-1000
B Grade: 551-700
C Grade: 401-550
D Grade: 251-400
E Grade: 1-250

The Jerseys

The General Classification (GC) is decided by the cumulative elapsed time taken to complete all seven stages. The Team Classification is based on the combined time of each team's fastest three riders on every stage.
The Sprintteri and Vuorikauris (Mountain Goat) classifications are determined by a rider's cumulative time through all designated Sprint and KOM/QOM segments of Stages 2 to 7. Where a stage includes the same segment multiple times, only the rider's fastest time through that segment will count toward the classification.

The Johtaja (leader in Finnish) classification is decided by the cumulative elapsed time taken to complete all seven stages in each age category.

Upgrade Information

Riders who upgrade during the first six stages will be classified in their higher grade.  Riders who upgrade in Stage 7 will not be re-classified.

Further Information

Open events using Zwift’s Racing Score with separate results for Men and Women.
Each event is a mass start with all riders visible on the course.
TT bikes are mandatory for the iTT. Draft will be disabled.
Z Power and riders without heart rate data will be excluded from the results.
A rider's best time will count if they race the same stage in multiple zones.
To be included in the GC riders must have a Zwiftpower profile.
Team GC will be based on each team’s fastest three riders.

description:
Team Intermountain was originally founded 11 years ago by 5 friends that rode together. name: RCC Global Club Ride
description:
WELCOME TO THE RAPHA CYCLING CLUB WORLD WIDE GROUP RIDE. 
 
This is a social group workout; a chance every week for members to get together from around the globe, ride, chat and support each other - it’s run as a group workout session with ‘keep everyone together’ enabled so no matter what your pace you’ll stay in the pack - it’s not a race or competition and open for anyone to join us. 
We host 4 rides every week on a Tuesday to suit different time zones around the world (aimed at evenings), join whichever time works best for you. 
 
WHO IS THE RCC?
 
The Rapha Cycling Club (RCC) is, as the name suggests, Rapha’s Cycling Club. The RCC exists to help connect like minded riders from all over the world, underpinned by Rapha’s products and experiences. We ride together across continents and here united within Zwift. 
 
For more information head to: www.Rapha.cc/rcc
 
RIDE LEADERS
 
The rides are led by our friendly team of member ride leaders from around the world.  The Leader (who has a yellow beacon over their head) will ride at a steady pace as set by the workout session. Prompts will appear on screen set by the workout designer Matt Rowe so you know what to do throughout the ride. On most occasions we will have a support ride leader (who will also have a beacon), the ride leaders are there to help support you and keep the banter going - to join the chat use the Zwift Companion smartphone app. 
 
ABOUT GROUP WORKOUTS
 
Zwifters line up in the starting area just like a normal event and once the event starts, workout mode begins. Everyone stays together regardless of power output. That's right, if you're outputting 100W and another Zwifter is outputting 400W you will stay in exactly the same position relative to each other. Only if you stop pedaling and fall 6 meters behind the group will the rubber-banding stop.
 
ABOUT THIS WORKOUT

Today's workout contains 4 x 6 minute blocks of Zone 3, with some surges thrown in for good measure! The Zone 3 riding should feel nice and comfortable, however the surges may sting a little. The surges in each block are only 20 seconds long, but at 110% of FTP so require a focused increase in effort .At the end of each 6 minute block, there is a 1 minute 'Free Ride' - this is your chance to turn an endurance based session into something special! Come event day or when riding with friends, it's likely you want some more power for that final sprint to the cafe right? Give it 100% in each 60 second Free Ride section to help you become more explosive! Stress points 45: #Social
 
 
WORKOUT DESIGNER
 
Matt Rowe is the founder of Rowe & King Coaching (www.roweandking.com) with 25 years of cycling experience, coaching amateur cyclists all over the world to  achieve their personal goals.
 
HELPFUL HINT
 
We highly recommend doing one of the FTP tests as the estimated FTP can be inaccurate and make the difficulty level of the workouts too high for your current fitness level.
You can adjust the difficulty of the workout mid-ride if needed, by using the up/down arrows on the left hand side, under the workout details.
 
HAVE FUN AND ENJOY THE RIDE.

#rcc

name: SISU Punainen - Stage 4
description:
SISU Racing launches its boldest challenge yet: SISU Punainen, a Vuelta-inspired, seven-stage race series built for riders who thrive when the road tilts skyward. Set entirely in Watopia, this inaugural edition is unapologetically brutal, beautifully relentless, and designed for the mountain goats of the virtual peloton.

Riders will compete for three individual classifications, ensuring every stage offers something to race for. The coveted Punainen (red in FInnish) Jersey rewards the overall General Classification leader based on cumulative elapsed time across all seven stages. The Sprintteri Jersey recognises the fastest riders through the designated sprint segments, while the Vuorikauris (Mountain Goat) Jersey celebrates the strongest climbers.  Whether you're an all-rounder, a sprinter or a pure climber, there's a jersey to chase.
Just like the Vuelta, SISU Punainen rewards courage, consistency, and climbing prowess.

For more information, and results, visit sisu.racing/punainen.

The Stages

Stage 1
Hilly Route, Watopia (Individual Time Trial)
Sat 22 & Sun 23 August

Stage 2
Mayan San Remo, Watopia
Tue 25 & Wed 26 August

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 3
Three Little Sisters, Watopia
Sat 29 & Sun 30 August

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 4
Climbers Gambit, Watopia
Tue 1 & Wed 2 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 5
Big Loop, Watopia
Sat 5 & Sun 6 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 6
Mountain 8, Watopia
Tue 8 & Wed 9 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 7
Mountain Route, Watopia
Sat 12 & Sun 13 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather, Aero or Anvil


Zwift Race Score

In our ongoing effort to keep the racing scene fresh and competitive, the upcoming SISU Punainen series is embracing Zwift's flexible new Zwift Racing Score (ZRS) framework!
Following a format similar to the recent Zwift Tour Fever series, this shift away from standard Category boundaries allows us to create tighter, more closely matched fields.

What this means for you:

A Shakeup in the Pack: If you usually find yourself stuck in the middle of a traditional category, this is your chance to step up, animate the race, and battle for the win.
New Challenges for Front-Runners: Former category leaders will be pushed to find new limits against a freshly recalibrated field.
Dynamic Racing Throughout: While the elite action in A Grade will remain as fierce as ever, expect highly competitive, unpredictable, and dynamic racing across the board - especially in Cat D Grade and expanded E Grade!

A Grade: 701-1000
B Grade: 551-700
C Grade: 401-550
D Grade: 251-400
E Grade: 1-250

The Jerseys

The General Classification (GC) is decided by the cumulative elapsed time taken to complete all seven stages. The Team Classification is based on the combined time of each team's fastest three riders on every stage.
The Sprintteri and Vuorikauris (Mountain Goat) classifications are determined by a rider's cumulative time through all designated Sprint and KOM/QOM segments of Stages 2 to 7. Where a stage includes the same segment multiple times, only the rider's fastest time through that segment will count toward the classification.

The Johtaja (leader in Finnish) classification is decided by the cumulative elapsed time taken to complete all seven stages in each age category.

Upgrade Information

Riders who upgrade during the first six stages will be classified in their higher grade.  Riders who upgrade in Stage 7 will not be re-classified.

Further Information

Open events using Zwift’s Racing Score with separate results for Men and Women.
Each event is a mass start with all riders visible on the course.
TT bikes are mandatory for the iTT. Draft will be disabled.
Z Power and riders without heart rate data will be excluded from the results.
A rider's best time will count if they race the same stage in multiple zones.
To be included in the GC riders must have a Zwiftpower profile.
Team GC will be based on each team’s fastest three riders.

name: Endurance Beat Pro
description:
Description:
This workout is designed to build your aerobic endurance while maintaining a steady and manageable effort. It consists of a long warm-up, steady state intervals at endurance pace, and a cool-down. Ideal for riders aiming to improve their long-distance capabilities without overreaching.

Structure:
• Warm-Up:
• 10 minutes starting easy and gradually increasing to 55% of FTP.
• Main Set:
• 40 minutes at 70–80% of FTP (Endurance Zone),
• 2:30/3:00 minutes of easy pedaling (55% FTP) between each 40-minute block.
• Cool-Down:
• 10 minutes gradually decreasing effort to % of FTP.

Key Points:
• Focus on maintaining a smooth, efficient pedal stroke.
• Keep your cadence steady between 85–95 rpm.
• Breathing should be controlled; you should be able to hold a conversation during the main intervals.
• Nutrition and hydration are important for sessions lasting over an hour.
Key Elements
Ideal for building aerobic endurance
Keeps attention high thanks to gentle variations
Great for indoor sessions focused on continuous worklink

name: WTRL Duathlon Opt1 BIKE
description:
WTRL's Duathlon League offers a unique and thrilling racing experience by combining biking on Zwift with the choice of running on Zwift or outside in real life. This makes it accessible to everyone and the ultimate test of racing versatility!

The series takes place every Wednesday year-round, allowing you to compete solo or for your club (or both!), with results and monthly leagues organized by age group, gender, and Zwift Club.

HOW DOES IT WORK?
You'll need to complete both the CYCLING and RUNNING events of the same option and complete at least 100m in each to record a score.

NO TREADMILL?
No problem! You can complete the run outside of Zwift. 
- Link your WTRL profile (www.wtrl.racing/profile/) to your Strava profile (Strava is free). 
- Sign-up for the Run Option through the Companion Zpp (but do not 'join the running event in-game). 
- Start and record your run on Strava within 5 minutes of finishing the bike ride, and we’ll handle the rest (your run score is usually processed within an hour).

FORMAT:
- 35 minutes of CYCLING 
- 7 minute 'Transition'
- 20 minutes of RUNNING

For full details, scoring, and registration, visit www.WTRL.racing/duathlon.

#wtrl #duathlon

name: Valhalla Fruitiful Team Chase
description:
Welcome to one of the most fascinating ride formats in the Zwift universe, the Valhalla Fruitiful Team Chase.
This is not a race, not a workout, but a pursuit ride of different groups, each with their own leaders, but in one world on one course.
Each team tries to keep to the advised lead-in and lap times to catch up with the team(s) ahead and/or escape the team(s) behind - like a cat and mouse chase! But it's not a race.
Respect your beacons, blob on yellow and help the reds! The better your team blobs, the faster you are.
There is a category for every rider of every level - so find your best fit of the ranges below and you will challenge yourself to a testing (but enjoyable) workout!
In a perfect world, we would blob up in the final kilometres for an epic mini-race, but this isn't always a perfect world. Help your team to not be left behind and to arrive at the afterparty on time.
To find out more about our rides, please visit our Valhalla Ride and Race Facebook group:
https://www.facebook.com/groups/503388660165279/

name: WTRL Duathlon Opt1 RUN
description:
WTRL's Duathlon League offers a unique and thrilling racing experience by combining biking on Zwift with the choice of running on Zwift or outside in real life. This makes it accessible to everyone and the ultimate test of racing versatility!

The series takes place every Wednesday year-round, allowing you to compete solo or for your club (or both!), with results and monthly leagues organized by age group, gender, and Zwift Club.

HOW DOES IT WORK?
You'll need to complete both the CYCLING and RUNNING events of the same option and complete at least 100m in each to record a score.

NO TREADMILL?
No problem! You can complete the run outside of Zwift. 
- Link your WTRL profile (www.wtrl.racing/profile/) to your Strava profile (Strava is free). 
- Sign-up for the Run Option through the Companion Zpp (but do not 'join the running event in-game). 
- Start and record your run on Strava within 5 minutes of finishing the bike ride, and we’ll handle the rest (your run score is usually processed within an hour).

FORMAT:
- 35 minutes of CYCLING 
- 7 minute 'Transition'
- 20 minutes of RUNNING

For full details, scoring, and registration, visit www.WTRL.racing/duathlon.

#wtrl #duathlon

name: 3R Octane Interval Ride [~3.2-3.6 w/kg avg]
description:
This is a 3R Group Ride Event. 3R Octane runs five days a week and is designed to provide a solid and fun training platform for riders.

Different ride leaders target different effort levels and courses, with power averages in the range 3.2-3.8 W/kg.

The wide spread reflects the diversity of rides, including weekly recovery, or transitional, rides which are usually on a Monday. Short, high intensity intervals, longer sweetspot intervals, flying laps, long and short climbs and exploring little used routes all feature.

The rides are typically around an hour long, but some can be up to two hours long, and all end with a mini race.

The Group welcomes rider interaction through messaging and the Octane discord server and features a super bunch of regulars to which newcomers, and riders stepping up from lower intensity rides, are always welcome. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/

name: 3R Spark: The Taylor Zwift Fan Club
description:
Welcome to the Taylor Zwift Fan Club, in partnership with 3R. Come and join us for the live version of the popular podcast about all the things that matter and a lot of things that don’t. Podcast hosts Tim and MP will be leading the ride and livestreaming from twitch.tv/TaylorZwiftFC – tune in!
The ride itself is a steady-state session where we split into two groups. Expect a sociable session with lots to keep you entertained. It’s not a race.
3R Spark runs five days a week and is designed to be an accessible and sociable training session, aimed primarily at riders in Cat-D. Different ride leaders target different effort levels and courses, with power averages in the range 2.0-2.5 W/kg. The wide spread reflects the diversity of rides. Mondays and Tuesdays are our entry-level steady-state rides, where we aim to hold a steady 2.0-2.2 throughout. Thursdays and Fridays are our interval sessions, designed to help Cat D riders push themselves a little further. For interval sessions we aim to average between 2.2-2.5 for the session, but there will be times above and below. Thursday and Friday sessions often include an optional mini-race at the end. Spark is a great introduction to group rides on Zwift, we are a friendly and supportive group who love to see one another succeed. We always have a sweeper (red beacon) whose wheel you can grab if you get dropped. There’s always plenty of good chat, via in-ride messages or on Discord. Come and join us! Join the 3R Facebook group for more info: https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/ #Team3R #3R #RideRaceRaise

name: 3R VOLT Interval Ride [~2.6-3.2 w/kg avg]
description:
This is a 3R Group Ride so please follow the leader beacon's (Yellow) instructions and if you are feeling strong, please help the keeper beacon (Red) to assist other riders back to the pack. 3R VOLT runs five days a week and is designed to provide a solid and fun training platform for riders.

Different ride leaders target different effort levels and courses, with power averages in the range 2.8-3.2 w/kg.

The wide spread reflects the diversity of rides and training needs, the following is a typical week:
Monday – After what has hopefully been a fun backed weekend on the bike, this our recovery session
Tuesday – Tends to be more of a classic interval session, riders usually finish with an average of around 3.0w/kg
Wednesday – We take to the hills and one of our tougher sessions with riders averaging around 3.2w/kg
Thursday – is our no red beacon ride and again tough interval sets and riders finishing around 3.2w/kg
Friday - is a little different, we don't take ourselves too seriously and often play a variety of games and quizzes along side the intervals and riders end up with around 2.8-3.0w/kg

The rides are typically around an hour long, but some may take up to 75mins with the majority finishing with either a ramp or a mini race.

The group welcomes rider interaction through messaging and the VOLT discord server and features a friendly bunch of regulars to which newcomers, and riders stepping up from lower intensity rides, are always welcome. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/

This group ride is not a race so. We welcome any feedback on our Facebook page https://www.facebook.com/groups/ClubWorldBicycleRelief/ #Team3R #Ride3R #RideRaceRaise.

name: Mountain Massif structured training:  Interval Training
description:
Created by Matteo Cigala, from Cigala Cycling, this structured training session is designed to help you cycle at a higher intensity.  For coaching and all your training needs visit https://coaching.cigalacycling.com/trainsmarterridefaster

About the session:
This session targets aerobic readiness, threshold control, and anaerobic repeatability. The structure blends steady-state work, controlled intensity changes, and high-output Tabata intervals to stress both aerobic and anaerobic systems while maintaining quality through structured recoveries.
Session details:
Warm Up 
10 minutes 40–65% CP 100–110 rpm
Main Set – 2 Rounds
3 minutes 80% CP Free cadence
1 minute 95% CP Free cadence
1 minute recovery 50–60% CP 100–110 rpm

Recovery 
5 minutes 50–60% CP 100–110 rpm


Intervals Sets – 2 Rounds Each round contains 8 repetitions of:
20 seconds 170% CP Free cadence
10 seconds 30% CP Free cadence
5 minutes recovery between rounds 50–60% CP 100–110 rpm
Cool Down 
10 minutes 40–55% CP 100–110 rpm
Total Time: 52 minutes 
Key coaching cues:
Keep the warm up smooth and relaxed to prepare for early intensity changes. Hold steady, controlled power during the 80% and 95% efforts — no surging. Use the short recoveries to reset breathing and cadence before the next block. During the 20-second high-power reps, stay seated, stay stable, and hit clean, repeatable accelerations. Keep the 10-second easy sections truly easy to maintain quality across all eight reps. Use the longer recoveries between rounds to bring heart rate down and restore control.

Safety Note: 
Only undertake vigorous exercise if you are fit and healthy to do so. If you are at all unsure, consult a Physician or Doctor first. All training equipment including Bikes and Turbo trainers should be in full working order. Do not use any piece of equipment that does not come up to the required standard.
More information:
For more information check out the Mountain Massif website www.mountainmassif.com, follow on Instagram @mountain_massif, Facebook @mountainmassif and join our Zwift Club, by clicking the following link https://www.zwift.com/clubs/mountainmassif/home
To record all your training data and chart your progress, consider using the TrainingPeaks app or Vekta by following the link https://joinvekta.com/

name: Rowe & King - Wednesday Wake-up
description:
ABOUT THIS WORKOUT

Rowe & King's Workout Wednesday is a moderate intensity workout to help build and maintain your aerobic engine. A session suitable for 12 months of the year.


WORKOUT DESIGNER

Matt Rowe / Rowe & King. Ex Pro Cyclist with experience racing over Europe and European Champion on the track as a Junior in 2005 is now a qualified coach of 11 years. Rowe & King founded in 2016 is a family business with coaches Luke Rowe - Team INEOS Racer, Dani Rowe (formally King) - Olympic Champion London 2016 and Courtney Rowe accompanying Matt along with a team of additional coaches. More info at www.roweandking.com

This is part of the Workout Wednesday live broadcast series with Matt Rowe on Zwift Community Live. 
ABOUT GROUP WORKOUTS

Zwifters line up in the starting area just like a normal event and once the event starts, workout mode begins. Everyone stays together regardless of power output. That's right, if you're outputting 100W and another Zwifter is outputting 400W you will stay in exactly the same position relative to each other. Only if you stop pedaling and fall 6 meters behind the group will the rubber-banding stop.

HELPFUL HINT

We highly recommend doing one of the FTP tests as the estimated FTP can be inaccurate and make the difficulty level of the workouts too high for your current fitness level. 

For more info on FTP go to: https://support.zwift.com/hc/en-us/articles/210208083-What-is-FTP-and-how-is-it-used-in-Zwift

name: SISU Punainen - Stage 4
description:
SISU Racing launches its boldest challenge yet: SISU Punainen, a Vuelta-inspired, seven-stage race series built for riders who thrive when the road tilts skyward. Set entirely in Watopia, this inaugural edition is unapologetically brutal, beautifully relentless, and designed for the mountain goats of the virtual peloton.

Riders will compete for three individual classifications, ensuring every stage offers something to race for. The coveted Punainen (red in FInnish) Jersey rewards the overall General Classification leader based on cumulative elapsed time across all seven stages. The Sprintteri Jersey recognises the fastest riders through the designated sprint segments, while the Vuorikauris (Mountain Goat) Jersey celebrates the strongest climbers.  Whether you're an all-rounder, a sprinter or a pure climber, there's a jersey to chase.
Just like the Vuelta, SISU Punainen rewards courage, consistency, and climbing prowess.

For more information, and results, visit sisu.racing/punainen.

The Stages

Stage 1
Hilly Route, Watopia (Individual Time Trial)
Sat 22 & Sun 23 August

Stage 2
Mayan San Remo, Watopia
Tue 25 & Wed 26 August

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 3
Three Little Sisters, Watopia
Sat 29 & Sun 30 August

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 4
Climbers Gambit, Watopia
Tue 1 & Wed 2 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 5
Big Loop, Watopia
Sat 5 & Sun 6 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 6
Mountain 8, Watopia
Tue 8 & Wed 9 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather or Aero

Stage 7
Mountain Route, Watopia
Sat 12 & Sun 13 September

PowerUps - Draft, Feather, Aero or Anvil


Zwift Race Score

In our ongoing effort to keep the racing scene fresh and competitive, the upcoming SISU Punainen series is embracing Zwift's flexible new Zwift Racing Score (ZRS) framework!
Following a format similar to the recent Zwift Tour Fever series, this shift away from standard Category boundaries allows us to create tighter, more closely matched fields.

What this means for you:

A Shakeup in the Pack: If you usually find yourself stuck in the middle of a traditional category, this is your chance to step up, animate the race, and battle for the win.
New Challenges for Front-Runners: Former category leaders will be pushed to find new limits against a freshly recalibrated field.
Dynamic Racing Throughout: While the elite action in A Grade will remain as fierce as ever, expect highly competitive, unpredictable, and dynamic racing across the board - especially in Cat D Grade and expanded E Grade!

A Grade: 701-1000
B Grade: 551-700
C Grade: 401-550
D Grade: 251-400
E Grade: 1-250

The Jerseys

The General Classification (GC) is decided by the cumulative elapsed time taken to complete all seven stages. The Team Classification is based on the combined time of each team's fastest three riders on every stage.
The Sprintteri and Vuorikauris (Mountain Goat) classifications are determined by a rider's cumulative time through all designated Sprint and KOM/QOM segments of Stages 2 to 7. Where a stage includes the same segment multiple times, only the rider's fastest time through that segment will count toward the classification.

The Johtaja (leader in Finnish) classification is decided by the cumulative elapsed time taken to complete all seven stages in each age category.

Upgrade Information

Riders who upgrade during the first six stages will be classified in their higher grade.  Riders who upgrade in Stage 7 will not be re-classified.

Further Information

Open events using Zwift’s Racing Score with separate results for Men and Women.
Each event is a mass start with all riders visible on the course.
TT bikes are mandatory for the iTT. Draft will be disabled.
Z Power and riders without heart rate data will be excluded from the results.
A rider's best time will count if they race the same stage in multiple zones.
To be included in the GC riders must have a Zwiftpower profile.
Team GC will be based on each team’s fastest three riders.

--------------------
SESSION FOCUS
--------------------
The focus of this session is to spend as much time as possible at and above ~90% of your VO2max. The priority is on maintaining high power/pace during the work intervals. These sessions are highly stressful but great for generating adaptations that will improve your oxygen-carrying capacity and therefore top-end aerobic capacity. For long-distance triathletes, these sessions can also serve as an effective precursor to longer interval sessions.
Key physiological adaptations we are hunting today:
- Increased maximal cardiac output to push more oxygenated blood each beat
- Greater mitochondrial density so every muscle fiber can process that oxygen
- Improved muscle oxygen extraction to keep power high deep into the set

This is an Innovation Cycling Training Ride Event – all riders are welcome. These events are put together to push you further than before, if you are feeling fresh hop on the front, if you need rest surf the draft. This training ride is part of the INC RELENTLESS training rides that happen daily with each day focusing on a different area of improvement. 

Tips: Use the draft to rest and ensure you do not lose the draft.

name: PACK Run: Step by Step + After Party
description:
New to running, coming back after some time off, or simply want a nice warm up or cool down session? Join us as we spend 30 minutes moving the legs in this slow-paced, social event. The goal of the event is to encourage folks to move.

The leader will average 8kph (7:30min/km) // 5mph (12min/mile) for the duration and it is expected everyone will stay together. This is a timed event, so we encourage runners to go at their own pace if the average pace is too fast and/or use a run/walk strategy.

**Note: if you utilize a run/walk strategy, please start with the walking portion so that you are not overrunning the group on each interval.**

Put your black and orange tops and socks on and let's get moving!

name: ROAD TO ZWIFT RACING LEAGUE
description:
Team up. Show up. Race together.

Zwift Racing League is team racing at its best: fast, sweaty, and addictive. Race alongside your teammates every Tuesday, combining teamwork, tactics, and competition with the kind of Type 2 Fun that keeps you coming back for more.

The 2026/27 season features four 6-week rounds from September to April, with new routes, a new format, XP rewards, and exclusive unlocks along the way. Round 1 gets underway on September 22.

YOUR ROAD TO ZRL STARTS HERE

Thinking about racing ZRL? This group ride is designed to show you what it’s all about and help you get ready for the start line.
Ride alongside other Zwifters as we introduce you to team racing, what to expect when you race ZRL, and how to take the next step and join a team.

There’s no racing today. Just ride with the group, learn more about ZRL, and get ready to race together.

READY TO RACE?

Once you've completed the ride, the next step is to find your team and get signed up.

Getting started is simple:

1 - Create your WTRL profile by connecting your Zwift account.
2 - Visit the ZRL Find a Team page for ways to find a team.
3 - Or register your own team and invite your friends.

REGISTER NOW
https://www.wtrl.racing/zwift-racing-league/

A reason not to hit snooze. Because friendly competition pulls us forward. The harder you go, the further she’ll get.

description:
Welcome to the Evolution Cycling Club [EVO] interval session. These rides are designed for Zwifters seeking a diverse, one-hour session that delivers a complete five-zone workout. You can draft within the pack to maintain

Zones 1–3, or push to the front and participate in sprints to hit Zones 4 and 5 during short bursts.

Our group thrives on high social interaction, so bring your best banter! Please use the mobile app or a keyboard to chat during the ride.
